records.title: Nobel Prizes 2026 at a glance
records.n: nobel prizes 2026 at a glance nobel prizes 2026 at a glance all six 2026 prizes in one table: who won, when it was announced, and what for. announced 5 to 12 october 2026 medicine on 5 october, physics on 6 october, chemistry on 7 october, literature on 8 october, peace on 9 october, economic sciences on 12 october. medicine: karl deisseroth, peter hegemann and georg nagel, for light-gated ion channels and optogenetics. physics: francis halzen, for icecube and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin. chemistry: henri b. kagan and kenso soai, for non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis. literature: anne carson, a canadian poet and writer. peace: navanethem "navi" pillay, for her efforts to promote peace and international law. economic sciences: robert e. hall and michael woodford, for microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation. the physics, chemistry, literature and economics reports give the prize as 12 million swedish crowns, about $1.2 million. the official nobelprize.org pages could not be read by automated tools in this check. names, citations and dates come from news reports that quote the committees. check the official pages before you use exact wording in notes.; one nobel page in search still showed the 2026 physics prize as not yet awarded. that page was out of date. the reuters-carried report and the official laureate listing say it was awarded on 6 october. general science and technology, digital technology and intellectual property; records.title: Physics: Francis Halzen and the IceCube neutrino detector
records.n: physics: francis halzen and the icecube neutrino detector physics: francis halzen and the icecube neutrino detector one laureate, for helping find very energetic neutrinos that come from cosmic sources. physics prize announced 6 october 2026 laureate: francis halzen, a belgian-american particle physicist. sole laureate. citation as reported: "for decisive contributions to the icecube neutrino observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin". prize: 12 million swedish crowns, about $1.2 million (reuters-carried report). the reports did not explain icecube or neutrinos. the background lines are general definitions, not from the reports.; the reports do not name halzen's institution, so none is given here. check the official laureate page. general science and technology, digital technology and intellectual property; science-general-tech-ipr; prelims-gs1; mains-gs3; the article explains high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and the icecube observatory.

records.title: Medicine: switching nerve cells on and off with light
records.n: medicine: switching nerve cells on and off with light medicine: switching nerve cells on and off with light three scientists share the prize for light-gated ion channels, the basis of optogenetics. medicine prize announced 5 october 2026 laureates, shared equally: karl deisseroth (stanford university, united states), peter hegemann (humboldt university, berlin) and georg nagel (university of wurzburg, germany). the work: light-gated ion channels. these are proteins that open when light hits them and let charged particles through. the use: optogenetics. light switches nerve cells on or off, so a researcher can control single cells. the committee said the method "is now being used in laboratories around the world to reveal the brain's mysteries". the ap report gives affiliations and ages but not nationalities. the citation wording above is the committee's statement as quoted in the report. check the official page for the formal citation. health, biotechnology, vaccines and biomedical technology; science-health-biotech; prelims-gs1; mains-gs3; the article explains light-gated ion channels and optogenetics as a biomedical research method.

records.title: Chemistry: how mirror-image molecules might end up one-sided
records.n: chemistry: how mirror-image molecules might end up one-sided chemistry: how mirror-image molecules might end up one-sided two chemists, for showing how a tiny imbalance can get amplified into a strong one-sided outcome. chemistry prize announced 7 october 2026 laureates, shared: henri b. kagan (universite paris-sud, orsay, france, aged 95) and kenso soai (tokyo university of science, aged 76). citation as quoted: "for the discovery of non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis". prize: 12 million swedish crowns, about $1.2 million. medals are presented in stockholm on 10 december. the reports did not give a full plain-english explanation of homochirality. the explanation above combines the reports with general definitions. lines marked background are general definitions.; ages come from chemistry world and afp. reuters, which one report cited, could not be read automatically. affiliations come from search summaries and the khaleej times report. general science and technology, digital technology and intellectual property; science-general-tech-ipr; prelims-gs1; mains-gs3; the article explains chirality, autocatalysis and asymmetric organic synthesis.

records.title: Literature: Anne Carson and the classical tradition
records.n: literature: anne carson and the classical tradition literature: anne carson and the classical tradition a canadian poet and writer. her work mixes verse, prose, translation and performance. literature prize announced 8 october 2026 laureate: anne carson, canadian poet and writer. born in toronto. icelandic citizenship since 2022. aged 76. swedish academy citation: "for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature". prize: 12 million swedish crowns, about $1.2 million (report). the official nobel page for the 2026 literature prize could not be read automatically. the citation above is as quoted in the khaleej times report. awards and honours: laureates, prizes and civilian distinctions; awards-honours; prelims-gs1; the article is a current-affairs note on the nobel literature distinction; the link is to the award fact, not to indian art and culture.

records.title: Peace: Navi Pillay and the rule of law
records.sub: Peace prize announced 9 October 2026 in Oslo
records.n: peace: navi pillay and the rule of law peace: navi pillay and the rule of law a former un human rights chief, honoured for work on peace and international law. peace prize announced 9 october 2026 in oslo laureate: navanethem "navi" pillay, aged 85. the reports say she was born in durban, south africa, to a family of tamil heritage. committee citation: "efforts to promote peace and international law". the committee also praised her "firm moral compass". positions: former un high commissioner for human rights. she has also served as a judge ad hoc at the international court of justice in the gambia v. myanmar, a case under the genocide convention (un biography). nominations: 287 candidates this year, 208 individuals and 79 organisations (as reported). the khaleej times headline calls pillay "indian-origin". the article body says she was born in south africa to a family with tamil roots. this note follows the body.; the un biography confirms that she sat as a judge ad hoc at the icj in the gambia v. myanmar. do not describe her as a permanent icj judge. international relations, groupings, summits and treaties; ir-groupings; prelims-gs1; mains-gs2; the article discusses the un human-rights role and an international court of justice case under the genocide convention, a direct international-relations and institution link.

records.title: Economics: Hall and Woodford on steadying the economy

records.title: Fields Medal 2026: four mathematicians at the Philadelphia congress
records.n: fields medal 2026: four mathematicians at the philadelphia congress fields medal 2026: four mathematicians at the philadelphia congress the top prize in mathematics went to four researchers, announced at the international congress of mathematicians. announced 23 july 2026 announced at the opening of the international congress of mathematicians (icm), philadelphia, on 23 july 2026. the congress ran until 30 july. winners: yu deng (university of chicago), john pardon (stony brook university), jacob tsimerman (university of toronto), hong wang (new york university and ihes, france). ages as reported: deng and pardon 37, tsimerman 38, wang 35. work areas: hong wang, in harmonic analysis and geometric measure theory (imu citation). deng in partial differential equations, pardon in symplectic geometry, tsimerman in algebraic geometry (as reported). one aggregator report says the names leaked early through a glitch on the icm website. that was not verified, so it is not stated here as fact. awards and honours: laureates, prizes and civilian distinctions; awards-honours; prelims-gs1; the article is a current-affairs note on the fields medal and its laureates; the link is to the award fact, not to general science and technology.

records.title: Artemis II: the first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit since 1972
records.n: artemis ii: the first crewed flight beyond low earth orbit since 1972 artemis ii: the first crewed flight beyond low earth orbit since 1972 four astronauts flew a crewed lunar flyby and came home safely. it tested the systems for the later landing. flight in april 2026 crew: reid wiseman, victor glover, christina koch and jeremy hansen. launched 1 april 2026. splashdown was 10 april 2026 (nasa mission page). it was the first crewed flight beyond low earth orbit since apollo 17 in 1972. the lunar flyby used a free-return trajectory. that brings the spacecraft back toward earth without a major engine burn. nasa still fired smaller burns. the final one lasted 8 seconds and changed orion's speed by 4.2 feet per second, pushing it toward earth before splashdown (nasa mission blog). at closest approach the crew was 4,067 miles above the lunar surface. at its farthest, the spacecraft was 252,756 miles from earth (nasa post-mission account). nasa called it a crewed systems validation test. the data feeds planning for artemis iii, a planned south-pole landing. most of these reports are news and aggregator pieces. nasa's own mission pages are the primary source for dates and distances. science and technology: space missions and programmes; science-space; prelims-gs1; mains-gs3; the article covers a crewed lunar mission, its trajectory and spacecraft systems testing.

records.title: AI Impact Summit 2026: the New Delhi Declaration
records.sub: Summit held in February 2026, New Delhi
records.n: ai impact summit 2026: the new delhi declaration ai impact summit 2026: the new delhi declaration india hosted a global ai summit in february 2026. the main outcome is a non-binding declaration built on seven pillars. summit held in february 2026, new delhi venue: bharat mandapam, new delhi. the pib release gives the summit dates as 18 to 19 february 2026. the declaration was gathered in new delhi on 19 february. outcome: the new delhi declaration on ai impact, built on the principle "welfare for all, happiness for all". endorsements: 92 countries and international organisations, according to the pib release. earlier news reports gave 88, 89 or 91. seven pillars: democratising ai resources; economic growth and social good; secure and trusted ai; ai for science; access for social empowerment; human capital development; resilient, efficient and innovative ai systems. framing: three "sutras", people, planet and progress. earlier reports gave 88, 89 and 91 endorsers. this note uses the pib figure of 92.; one source names follow-on platforms that came out of the declaration. only one source reports them, so they are left out here. general science and technology, digital technology and intellectual property; science-general-tech-ipr; prelims-gs1; mains-gs3; the declaration addresses ai systems, access, trust, science and technology policy.; international relations, groupings, summits and treaties; ir-groupings; prelims-gs1; mains-gs2; the article reports a new delhi declaration endorsed by countries and international organisations at a global summit.

records.title: Union Budget 2026-27: the key numbers
records.n: union budget 2026-27: the key numbers union budget 2026-27: the key numbers presented on 1 february 2026. the fiscal targets, the big allocations and the new schemes. presented 1 february 2026 presented by finance minister nirmala sitharaman on 1 february 2026. reports describe the theme as "yuva shakti". total expenditure: about ₹53.47 lakh crore, about 7.7% above the revised estimate for 2025-26 (prs). capital expenditure: about ₹12.2 lakh crore. fiscal deficit target: 4.3% of gdp for fy27, down from 4.4%. nominal gdp growth assumed at 10%. health ministry allocation: about ₹1,06,530 crore, nearly 10% above the revised estimate. income tax slabs unchanged for assessment year 2026-27. most figures come from secondary explainers and the prs analysis. the key budget figures were checked against pib. for anything exact, use the budget speech and pib. economy: growth, fiscal policy, budget, rbi and monetary policy; economy-macro; prelims-gs1; mains-gs3; the article focuses on fiscal deficit, expenditure, capital spending and budget allocations.

records.title: Padma Awards 2026: 131 honours
records.n: padma awards 2026: 131 honours padma awards 2026: 131 honours announced on 25 january 2026, on the eve of republic day. the list covers the three civilian tiers and includes posthumous honours. announced 25 january 2026 total: 131 awards. five padma vibhushan, 13 padma bhushan and 113 padma shri, per the mha list. padma vibhushan (as reported): dharmendra singh deol and v s achuthanandan, both posthumously; k t thomas (public affairs); n rajam (art); p narayanan (literature and education). padma bhushan (as reported): alka yagnik (singer), mammootty (actor), uday kotak (industrialist), vijay amritraj (tennis), bhagat singh koshyari, and piyush pandey and shibu soren, both posthumously. breakdown reported: 19 women, 16 posthumous awardees and 6 foreigners, nris, pios or oci cardholders. the mha list (25 january 2026) gives 131 awards, with two duo cases counted as one award each. names above come from news reports, so check the mha list before you quote one. awards and honours: laureates, prizes and civilian distinctions; awards-honours; prelims-gs1; the article covers padma civilian honours, their three tiers and the annual award list.

records.title: RBI raises repo rate to 5.50%: the first hike since February 2023
records.n: rbi raises repo rate to 5.50%: the first hike since february 2023 rbi raises repo rate to 5.50%: the first hike since february 2023 the mpc moved the repo rate up by 25 basis points. the vote on the rate was unanimous; the change of stance was not. decided 7 october 2026 repo rate raised by 25 basis points, from 5.25% to 5.50%, under the liquidity adjustment facility (laf). the mpc voted unanimously on the rate. standing deposit facility (sdf) rate: 5.25%. marginal standing facility (msf) rate, also the bank rate: 5.75% (rbi release). the mpc also changed the stance from neutral to "calibrated tightening". two members, dr nagesh kumar and prof ram singh, wanted the stance to stay neutral (rbi release). projections: real gdp growth for 2026-27 at 7.1%; cpi inflation for 2026-27 at 5.2% (rbi release). the 63rd mpc meeting ran from 5 to 7 october 2026. the next meeting is scheduled for 2 to 4 december 2026 (rbi release). the minutes of the meeting were due after this check, so any detail from the minutes is not covered here. economy: growth, fiscal policy, budget, rbi and monetary policy; economy-macro; prelims-gs1; mains-gs3; the article covers repo rates, the monetary policy committee, inflation and growth projections.

records.title: Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Act, 2026
records.n: public examinations (prevention of unfair means) amendment act, 2026 public examinations (prevention of unfair means) amendment act, 2026 parliament passed the amendment in the monsoon session and the president gave assent on 31 july 2026. it covers upsc, so every aspirant should know what it does. act no. 10 of 2026, assent 31 july 2026 act no. 10 of 2026, assented to on 31 july 2026. it amends the public examinations (prevention of unfair means) act, 2024 (gazette text, as transcribed by a non-government site; the e-gazette pdf was not reachable from the build environment). the act amends section 12 so that investigation can be handed to a special task force that the central government constitutes by notification. where a special task force is constituted, only it investigates. investigations must be completed within two months, counted from the date of the information (or the reference or notification to the central investigating agency or the special task force). each state government and union territory administration, after consulting the chief justice of the high court, designates a court of session as a special fast track court, by notification. trials proceed day-to-day, and special public prosecutors are appointed for these courts. trials must be completed within three months of the chargesheet being filed, or, for an already-pending transferred case, of its receipt by the designated court. appeals lie to the high court against a judgment, sentence or order of these courts that is not interlocutory, and are heard by a bench of two high court judges. the high court may also hear separate appeals against orders granting or refusing bail. an appeal is filed within thirty days of the judgment, sentence or order appealed against, which the high court may extend for sufficient cause, but no appeal is entertained after ninety days. the appeal is to be disposed of within three months of its admission, as far as possible. the penalties are revised. the figures in the bill as introduced are in the prs summary. check the enacted sections 10 to 12 for the final numbers. the act text here is a transcription on a non-government site. the official gazette record is cg-dl-e-31072026-275035 (egazette.gov.in). use the official pdf for exact wording before quoting it in an answer. governance: institutions, schemes, public policy and centre–state relations; polity-governance; prelims-gs1; mains-gs2; the act changes investigation, trial and appeal arrangements for public examinations, including upsc examinations.

records.title: Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2026
records.sub: Act No. 14 of 2026, assent 11 August 2026, deemed in force from 16 May 2026
records.n: supreme court (number of judges) amendment act, 2026 supreme court (number of judges) amendment act, 2026 raises the maximum number of supreme court judges, other than the chief justice, from 33 to 37. it replaces the ordinance of 16 may 2026, and it was deemed in force from that date. act no. 14 of 2026, assent 11 august 2026, deemed in force from 16 may 2026 act no. 14 of 2026, assented to on 11 august 2026. deemed to have come into force on 16 may 2026 (gazette text, as transcribed by a non-government site). amends section 2 of the supreme court (number of judges) act, 1956, replacing "thirty-three" with "thirty-seven". the maximum number of supreme court judges, other than the chief justice, goes from 33 to 37. repeals the supreme court (number of judges) amendment ordinance, 2026. anything done under the ordinance is treated as done under the 1956 act as amended. introduced in lok sabha on 20 july 2026 (prs). pib's monsoon session summary says both houses passed it (pib, 13 august 2026). the act text is a transcription on a non-government site. the official gazette record is cg-dl-e-11082026-275379 (egazette.gov.in), which was not reachable from the build environment. indian polity: constitution, political system, amendments and judgments; polity-constitution; prelims-gs1; mains-gs2; the article covers the statutory number of supreme court judges and its constitutional basis under article 124.

records.title: Tribunals Reforms Act, 2026: the National Tribunals Commission
records.sub: Act No. 17 of 2026, assent 13 August 2026; all provisions in force 25 August 2026
records.n: tribunals reforms act, 2026: the national tribunals commission tribunals reforms act, 2026: the national tribunals commission assent on 13 august 2026. it repeals the 2021 tribunals law. the act provides for a national tribunals commission; its establishment date is to be appointed by a separate notification. act no. 17 of 2026, assent 13 august 2026; all provisions in force 25 august 2026 act no. 17 of 2026, assented to on 13 august 2026 (gazette text, as transcribed by a non-government site). all provisions came into force on 25 august 2026 under notification s.o. 4713(e) of the same date. section 3 provides that the national tribunals commission is established from a date that the central government appoints by notification in the official gazette. the notices read here do not give that establishment date. chairperson: a person who is or has been a supreme court judge or a chief justice of a high court. judicial members: a person who is or has been a chief justice or judge of a high court. technical members: at least 25 years of special knowledge and experience in public administration, finance, law, accountancy, banking, management or technology. functions include selection for tribunal vacancies, review of tribunal performance, inquiry into complaints about members' conduct, and a national tribunals data grid (bill as introduced, prs). the act text is a transcription on a non-government site. the official gazette record is cg-dl-e-13082026-275447 (egazette.gov.in), not reached from the build environment.; the establishment date under section 3 is not in the notices read here. the october rules notice (g.s.r. 856(e)) refers to the commission but does not set that date, per the zc-03 review. governance: institutions, schemes, public policy and centre–state relations; records.n: mines and minerals (development and regulation) amendment act, 2026: state levies on mineral rights mines and minerals (development and regulation) amendment act, 2026: state levies on mineral rights assent on 17 august 2026. it limits state levies on mineral rights and mineral-bearing land, with a new section 9d. it raises a federalism question and an equality question. act no. 20 of 2026, assent 17 august 2026; in force 22 august 2026 (per the zc-03 review) act no. 20 of 2026, assented to on 17 august 2026 (gazette text, as transcribed by a non-government site). inserts section 9d. a state levy on mineral rights or mineral-bearing land, whether based on quantity, value or royalty, is allowed only under conditions the central government prescribes. section 9d deems invalid any such levy that had not been deposited with the state government or recovered by it before the act's commencement. amounts already deposited or recovered are not refundable. section 13(2) is amended to cover the conditions or restrictions on levies under section 9d. a new definition of "mineral bearing land" is added to section 3. commencement: the central government appointed the date of publication of s.o. 4642(e), 22 august 2026, as the effective date. the transcription was checked; the official pdf was not reached. the act text is a transcription on a non-government site. the official gazette record is cg-dl-e-17082026-275519 (egazette.gov.in), not reached from the build environment. quote the act itself for exact wording. indian polity: constitution, political system, amendments and judgments; polity-constitution; prelims-gs1; mains-gs2; the article's central issue is parliament's limits on state levies and fiscal federalism.; economy: growth, fiscal policy, budget, rbi and monetary policy; economy-macro; prelims-gs1; mains-gs3; the act changes state revenue from mineral rights and mineral-bearing land.

records.title: Sukhna Wetland and Sauj Jheel join the Ramsar List
records.n: sukhna wetland and sauj jheel join the ramsar list sukhna wetland and sauj jheel join the ramsar list a 15 october announcement adds two very different wetlands: an urban-edge reservoir and a ganga floodplain lake. designation announced 15 october 2026 the convention on wetlands announced sukhna wetland and sauj jheel as new ramsar sites on 15 october. its release and the environment ministry put india’s announced total at 103. sukhna wetland (site 2602) lies beside chandigarh at the foot of the outer himalayas. it is a peri-urban reservoir whose catchment affects water and sediment flows. sauj jheel (site 2603) is a shallow lake in uttar pradesh’s ganga floodplain, near saman bird sanctuary. the convention describes it as a habitat for waterbirds and reports more than 30,000 birds there regularly. the convention on wetlands was adopted at ramsar, iran, in 1971 and entered into force in 1975. it entered into force for india on 1 february 1982. the pib announcement confirms the designation, locations and the announced total of 103. the cited convention article returned http 403 when opened here, so its site numbers, ecological details and proposed management actions were not independently checked in this review. the convention’s live india profile also showed an older total; use 103 as the announcement figure and recheck the live directory before calling it the current count. environment and ecology: species, protected areas and biodiversity; environment-ecology; prelims-gs1; mains-gs3; the note links two named wetlands and their site management to biodiversity and environment topics.

current operational status was not independently checked. cabinet approval announced 14 october 2026 the union cabinet approved ₹53,428 crore to continue the national social assistance programme from 2026–27 to 2030–31. the release says the approval covers 3.20 crore beneficiaries across all 36 states and union territories. the programme is to be called pradhan mantri samajik sahayata yojana. the approved component names include pradhan mantri vridhavastha pension yojana (old age), pradhan mantri vidhawa pension yojana (widow), pradhan mantri divyangjan pension yojana (disability) and pradhan mantri parivar labh yojana (family benefit). for disability pension, the approved assistance is ₹375 for ages 0–79 and ₹625 from age 80. the benchmark-disability threshold changes from 80% to 40%, and the minimum-age rule changes to cover people from birth. the cabinet release says guidelines setting the revised eligibility, coverage and assistance are to be issued and implemented within three months. article 41 of the constitution is the public-assistance directive. it asks the state to act within its economic capacity and development. the cabinet approved the changes, and its release says the revised guidelines are to be issued and implemented within three months. their current publication status has not been independently checked; records.n: the union ordinance stopwatch (art 123) m03 the union ordinance stopwatch (art 123) teach when an ordinance can be made, how long it lives, and what ends it. art 123(1)-(3) as read in mirrors; records.title: Article 200 gives the Governor three options: assent, reserve for the President, or withhold assent and return the Bill with a message. The first proviso quali…
records.limit: The Union argued four options; the Court preferred the three-option reading.

detail.text: Article 200 gives the Governor three options: assent, reserve for the President, or withhold assent and return the Bill with a message. The first proviso qualifies the word "withholds"; it does not create a fourth option, and the Governor cannot simply withhold and let the Bill die.
detail.note: The Union argued four options; the Court preferred the three-option reading.

detail.text: Holding H, c and other reserve behaviour fixed, increasing r or e lowers the multiplier. Holding H, r, e fixed, derivative of m with respect to c is (r+e-1)/(c+r+e)^2: negative if r+e<1 and zero if r+e=1. If H changes, model money can rise despite a falling multiplier. This is algebra under assumptions, not a causal forecast.

records.title: No board may be superseded or suspended for more than six months, and only on listed grounds (persistent default, negligence, acts prejudicial to members, stal…

detail.text: No board may be superseded or suspended for more than six months, and only on listed grounds (persistent default, negligence, acts prejudicial to members, stalemate, or failure of the election authority to hold elections). A board cannot be superseded at all where there is no Government shareholding, loan, financial assistance or guarantee. For a banking society the Banking Regulation Act also applies, and for a non-multi-State banking society the six months reads as one year. The administrator must hold elections within the period and hand over.
